<description>
When testing a hardware wallet integration, I found that when attempting to create a wallet with the wrong app open on the hardware wallet, the GUI crashes instead of showing an error message. After restarting, when attempting to create a wallet with the same name again, it fails with "Database already exists". Over RPC, there's no crash, but `createwallet` returns error code -1 and leaves the same files and directories behind.

This happens when setting up an external-signer wallet. When the signer fails, setting up the wallet throws `std::runtime_error`, and `CreateWallet()` doesn't catch it. The GUI's worker thread has no handler, so the uncaught exception ends in `std::terminate`, and RPC's catch-all turns it into error code -1. The directory and `wallet.dat` are created before setup and never removed when setup fails.

This uncaught exception has been encountered previously in bitcoin-core/gui#395, and bitcoin-core/gui#396 stopped the dialog from enabling the "External signer" option, but didn't handle the exception.

Commit 1 catches the exception as `LoadWalletInternal()` does. The GUI shows an error dialog, and RPC returns error code -4, with the message starting with "Wallet creation failed."
Commit 2 ensures that on failure, it removes only what was created. The cleanup also runs for failures that don't throw, e.g. an invalid `-addresstype`.

How to reproduce:
```
cmake -B build -DBUILD_GUI=ON && cmake --build build
build/bin/bitcoin-qt -regtest -datadir=$(mktemp -d) -signer="python3 test/functional/mocks/invalid_signer.py"
```

Then click File, Create Wallet, Create. "External signer" is already ticked and the name is pre-filled as `trezor_t`.

On master: `terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'`, the process aborts, and `trezor_t/wallet.dat` is left behind.
With the PR: a "Create wallet failed" dialog appears, a retry shows the same dialog, and nothing is left on disk.

The tests `CreateWalletSignerFailure` and `CreateWalletInvalidArgs` in `wallet_tests` create wallets through the wallet loader, which is the same call the GUI makes. `wallet_signer.py` now expects -4, and checks that a failed creation leaves nothing behind, that a retry fails the same way, and that a directory or files that already existed are kept.

You can see the tests fail without the fix:

```
git checkout HEAD~2 -- src/wallet/wallet.cpp
cmake --build build
build/bin/test_bitcoin --run_test=wallet_tests/CreateWalletSignerFailure,CreateWalletInvalidArgs
build/test/functional/wallet_signer.py
```
</description>
